ideas: OPUS_IDEAS.md (second and last Opus 5.5 medium consultation)
question: Does the retained shared-gamma KM equal-depth F_sub advantage over QAOA generalize to fresh iid disorder instances, survive independent optimizer repeats, and survive independent state reconstruction?
hamiltonian: sum_{i<j} J_ij Z_i Z_j + 0.1 sum_i X_i, J_ij iid Normal(0,1), open chain, no Kac rescaling (arXiv:2408.03251 author-code convention)
instances: J from SeedSequence([20261115, N, k]) normals over i<j in row order; k=0..3 must reproduce the R1 manifest hashes
no_filtering: every k in the lists is run and reported; incomplete instances are listed, never replaced

families.K: shared-gamma, nested seed provider for KM, 2+3L
families.nodata: shared-gamma, nested seed provider for K, 1+3L
families.qaoa_heavy: same circuit as qaoa; 27 L1 random starts and two draws per perturbation level per parent; control for search effort

parametrization_box: unchanged from R2: linear coefficients, every diagonal coefficient in [-2pi/s_J, 2pi/s_J], shells and beta in [-2pi, 2pi]
repeat_independence: repeat r changes: L1 random seeds SeedSequence([20261120,N,k,1,r,s]); grid offset u = pi (j + delta_r)/16 and c0 jitter +-0.05 from [20261121,N,k,r]; perturbation seeds [20261122,N,k,L,r,pid,j,d]; ramp jitter [20261123,N,k,L,r]; QAOA append-zero perturb [20261124,N,k,L,r,heavy]. Common random numbers across families within a repeat.
continuation: as R2: per parent interp + (append-zero for QAOA | time-rescaled for shared) + perturb 0.1 + perturb 0.3; two fresh ramps; QAOA best append-zero + N(0,0.05); nested K<-nodata, KM<-K
selection: energy only. Per repeat: lowest E in that repeat. Primary: best over repeats (lowest of the three). No ground state, eigenvector, E0 or fidelity enters optimization, starts, beam or selection.
primary_metric: F_sub, weight in the eigenspace within 1e-6 of E0 (all N)

claim.rho: log[(1 - F_QAOA)/(1 - F_KM)], each F clamped to <= 1 - 1e-9
claim.win: rho > log 1.1 and dF > 0.005; loss mirrored; otherwise tie. Tie 'both failed' if max F < 0.02. Tie 'unreachable' if the 1e-6 window contains no even-sector state. Joint win if also E_KM <= E_QAOA + 1e-6, otherwise fidelity-only.
claim.tests: one-sided exact sign test (ties excluded), one-sided Wilcoxon on rho, bootstrap 95% percentile CI of median rho and median dF (10000 resamples, seed 20261125), Holm over the three N at L=6
claim.criteria_per_N: (a) Holm-adjusted sign p < 0.05 at L6; (b) bootstrap lower bound of median rho > 0 at L6; (c) L5 unadjusted sign p < 0.05 and rho CI lower bound > 0; (d) (a) and (b) hold for at least 2 of 3 per-repeat selections and with qaoa_heavy replacing qaoa; replay gate passes at that N
claim.verdict: generalizes if all N pass; partial if some pass (failing N named); not supported if none. Never a statement of global optimality.

replay: independent code (replay_independent.py): J from seed, K and M features from definitions, sparse Pauli-string operators, expm_multiply evolution, eigsh ground space; all selected states of every repeat
reliability: reported separately: repeats at best energy, across-repeat F SD and range, E spread > 1e-4, equal-E different-F pairs, QAOA-heavy minus QAOA energy, nested-ancestor fraction, projected gradient at stop, monotonicity and KM<=K violations
bounds: report selected cells touching a bound, max |diag coeff| / box, starts touching a bound; no rerun
job_order: k_primary then k_secondary; within each k N=12, 9, 6; repeats inner
stop: single round; no re-tuning after viewing fidelities
